title: Budgeted refactoring optimizes changed-code smell score without metric gaming
query: We just shipped a feature and I want a max-budget cleanup pass. The changed files include one 220-line TypeScript handler with nested branching, weak tests, and duplicated validation. What should the refactoring workflow do?
reference_points: Routes to the refactoring skill rather than runtime-debugging or hardening as the primary owner.
Uses budget-advisor for the max budget and preserves the refactoring output contract.
Prioritizes changed/high-churn code with complexity, nesting, duplication, and coverage risk.
Requires behavior proof before and after structural changes.
Rejects raw line-count gaming and reports residual risk.

title: Refactoring rejects unapproved behavior changes
query: While refactoring a messy API module, the agent notices the API response shape is annoying. Should it change the response while it is cleaning up?
reference_points: States that refactoring preserves behavior unless an API migration is explicitly in scope.
Requires public contract and caller proof before changing response shape.
Treats the behavior change as a separate feature/API decision or ticket.
Keeps the refactor focused on structure, tests, duplication, and maintainability.
